title: Albion's Legacy - A Quintessential Dungeon Dive Game
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1vJB1yOPOf0

Daniel (@dungeondive) opens with a confession. He has sold Gloomhaven, Mage Knight, Tainted Grail and a shelf of other hits, yet spends his time on underdogs, which he calls a fantastic way to kill a YouTube channel. Now he's made a long video about Albion's Legacy, a 6.7-rated game from Thomas M. Gofton, Jasco Games and Lynnvander Studios that almost nobody searches for. He has lost every game he's played and can't stop thinking about it. He's also clear that this isn't a call to hunt it down: he got the deluxe second edition with every expansion for $75 at a Goodwill auction, and has seen one listed for $500.

Arthurian heroes leave Camelot by drawbridge, docks or sally port, and each exit only draws its own terrain until the regions connect. Victory takes quest coins plus a story quest before despair snuffs out Camelot's ten flames. Retiring a wounded knight costs a virtue but lets you bring in the right specialist. A hero standing in the War Room or the kitchen buffs everyone else, and the stables unlock mid-game to quicken the pace.

The threat decks give him great emergent moments: the dead rising inside Camelot, and Accolon of Gaul calling Arthur out at the drawbridge. His complaints are identical starting gear, combat-only threats, thin flavour text and unclear rules for failed challenges. He shares his house rules and hopes for a complete third edition. The game has even sent him off to read up on Arthurian legend.

----

Daniel loves a 6.7-rated game he has never beaten. What's the game you defend that the ratings (and your win record) say you shouldn't?
